newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian fishermen block part-foreign owned trawlers.
newsitem.headline: Indian fishermen block part-foreign owned trawlers.

text.p: Indian fishermen on Wednesday launched an indefinite blockade to stop part-foreign owned trawlers using harbours in nine states, their leaders said.

About 75 boats carrying nearly 2,000 fishermen sailed into the Arabian Sea to prevent foreign vessels from entering Bombay harbour, said Vijay Bhandarkar, president (Bombay region) of National Fish Workers' Forum.
"Most vessels, apparently warned, stayed in the high seas and did not venture to enter the harbour," Bhandarkar said.
He said police had prevented another 100 boats carrying protestors from putting to sea.
The fishermen were demanding the cancellation of deep-sea joint venture licences because, they say, the mechanised trawlers are depleting India's fishing grounds and represent unfair competition.
"Our protestors will sail out again tomorrow, though we hope to hear from the government during the day," Bhandarkar said.

Bhandarkar said the government had approved 33 joint ventures for deep sea fishing after it liberalised its economy in 1991, but an official committee had subsequently recommended cancellation of their licences.
"But nothing has been done so far to revoke their licences," Bhandarkar said.

"...we used to get a haul of two to three tonnes of fish a day. But in the last few years he have had to be at sea at least for a week to get half of what we used to get in the past," Bhandarkar said.
An official of the Bombay docks denied there had been any blockade of the harbour.
Bhandarkar said 7.5 million people were directly involved in fishing and another 50 million depended on the industry for their livelihood.
The Press Trust of India news agency, in a report from the south eastern port of Visakhapatnam said several vessels were prevented from entering its harbour.
